newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere profits up 81 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Solidere profits up 81 pct in 1996.

text.p: Solidere, the company at the heart of Lebanon's reconstruction, said on Monday its profits rose 81 percent in 1996 due to strong land sales in the war-damaged Beirut Central District it is rebuilding.
It also reported a strong cash position with no debt on the balance sheet and a 70 percent increase in revenues in the third year of the 25-year project.
A company spokesman said the results should help dispel recent rumours in Beirut that Solidere was short of cash and not making sales.

Issuing unaudited annual results for the first time since it began operations in 1994, Solidere said revenues rose to $74.2 million from $43.5 million and net revenues from real estate activities were $43.7 million, up from $12.2 million in 1995.
Net income was $58.5 million compared with the 1995 audited profit of $32.3 million, the company said.
According to the unaudited balance sheet, Solidere's cash position at January 1, 1997, was $328.4 million plus an additional $136 million receivables.

The results showed that Solidere achieved its business plan objectives for 1966 and "exceeded its revenue projections as a result of strong land sales in the Beirut Central District," the company said in a statement.
"The fact that our profits grew 81 percent in 1996 is a demonstration that the company is moving ahead on the right path," a spokesman said.
"It's clearly an inappropriate perception that the company has no cash," he added.

The company said plans for 1997 included completion of its first landmark development in central Beirut -- a multi-storey headquarters for the U.N.'s Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA).

Other major 1997 projects included completing restoration of nearly all buildings preserved in the city centre, launching a strong rental market and starting key projects like building new souks, a traditional housing project and several developments for the Lebanese government.
